mentions.name: Lightspeed
mentions.description: A self-hostable, multi-tenant AI agent harness built on durable workflow engines (currently supporting Temporal). Unlike agent harnesses that require a full OS process on your machine or a VM, it uses no compute while agents are paused yet aims to be as powerful as tools like Claude Code or Codex. It is positioned as a battery-included product rather than just another agent SDK.
mentions.problem: Most new agent harnesses must be hosted on a machine or VM, meaning the agent needs a full OS process at all times; there are no good harnesses that are multi-tenant, use no compute while paused, and remain as powerful as Claude Code or Codex.
mentions.source_excerpt:
A self-hostable Claude Tag or OAI Work [0].

A while ago, I realized that most new agent harnesses being built must be hosted on your machine or on a VM--in other words the agent needs a full OS process at all times.

But we do not have good harnesses being built that are multi-tenant, do not use compute while they are paused, but are are still as powerful as, say, Claude Code or Codex, OpenClaw.

So I set out to build one. I realized that the best substrate for these kind of agents are durable workflow engines. I'm currently supporting Temporal. AFAIK much of OAI agent infra is built on Temporal too. My harness is decidedly not just another agent SDK, but rather a battery-included product.

mentions.name: lightspeed
mentions.description: An agent harness for durable workflow runtimes, starting with Temporal. It runs long-running agents directly inside workflow code instead of requiring a guest OS and dedicated process, making them easier to operate and scale. Supports skills, MCP, prompts, and a virtual file system, with sandboxes planned; uses a content-addressable store (CAS) for payloads to keep the workflow code footprint lightweight.
mentions.problem: Most agents for durable workflows feel like toy examples—there is no 'Codex' or 'Claude Code' for runtimes like Temporal—and current frontier harnesses need to run inside a guest OS with a dedicated process, which is challenging to orchestrate and maintain.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Agent harness for durable workflows, starting with Temporal.

Most agents for durable workflows feel like toy examples. There is no "Codex" or "Claude Code" for, say, Temporal. So I'm building full-featured agent for these runtimes. Why? Because it makes long-running agents easier to operate and scale. Currently, all frontier harnesses need to run inside a guest OS and need a dedicated process, this is quite challenging to orchestrate and maintain.
